guides.statement: The Android install-options page lists guides for MaaS360, Microsoft Intune, MobileIron and Workspace ONE UEM; the Intune guide covers Android and Android on ChromeOS devices.

quotes: Deploying Zscaler Client Connector with MaaS360 for Android
Deploying Zscaler Client Connector with Microsoft Intune for Android
Deploying Zscaler Client Connector with MobileIron for Android
Deploying Zscaler Client Connector with Workspace ONE UEM for Android
With Microsoft Intune, you can deploy Zscaler Client Connector for your Android and Android on ChromeOS devices.

guide-versions.statement: The Android guides are written against Microsoft Intune service release 2006, MobileIron Core 10.1, Workspace ONE UEM 25.6.111.0 (2506) and MaaS360 10.72.

quotes: The Microsoft Intune Service release version 2006 is shown in the following steps.
The following deployment procedure is based on MobileIron Core 10.1.
The version used for the following steps is Workspace ONE UEM 25.6.111.0 (2506).
The following deployment procedure is based on MaaS360 10.72.

preconfigure-needs-ae.statement: The Intune guide says Client Connector can be preconfigured with parameters when deployed from Google Play with Android Enterprise enabled, and cannot be preconfigured when deployed from Google Play without Android Enterprise or as an APK file; the Workspace ONE and MaaS360 guides say the same. The MobileIron guide says Android Enterprise must first be enabled for MobileIron UEM before deploying.

quotes: If you deploy Zscaler Client Connector from Google Play with Android Enterprise enabled, you can preconfigure Zscaler Client Connector with parameters.
But, if you deploy Zscaler Client Connector from Google Play without Android Enterprise enabled or as an APK file, you cannot preconfigure Zscaler Client Connector.
If you deploy Zscaler Client Connector from Google Play without Android Enterprise enabled or as an APK file, you cannot preconfigure Zscaler Client Connector.
You can only preconfigure Zscaler Client Connector if you deploy the app from Google Play with Android Enterprise enabled.
Before deploying Zscaler Client Connector, you must first enable the Android Enterprise feature for MobileIron UEM.

apk.statement: The Workspace ONE guide says to download the Client Connector APK file from the Registered Devices > Android tab and to contact Zscaler Support to enable the APK file link. In the Intune guide an APK file is uploaded, Zscaler Support is contacted for a private APK file, and the app can take up to 10 minutes to publish and appear in private apps.

quotes: Download the Zscaler Client Connector APK file from the Registered Devices > Android tab.
Contact Zscaler Support to enable the APK file link.
APK file: Upload the APK file. Contact Zscaler Support for a private APK file.
The app can take up to 10 minutes to publish and appear in private apps.

min-os.statement: The Workspace ONE guide has the admin select Android 8.0 as the Minimum OS. The Workspace ONE and Intune guides say the minimum operating system for Android on ChromeOS is Android 6.0.
min-os.conditions: These are values the guides tell the admin to enter in the MDM, not a stated support matrix.

quotes: Minimum OS: Select Android 8.0.
The minimum operating system for Android on ChromeOS is Android 6.0.
The minimum operating system for Android on ChromeOS is Android 6.0.

always-on-vpn.statement: The Intune guide says Client Connector can restrict the traffic and secure the device before enrollment if Always ON VPN is enabled on the organization's MDM for the Zscaler app; after enrollment it intercepts the traffic and forwards it according to the Admin Console policies. In Intune this is a Device Restriction profile (Fully Managed, Dedicated, and Corporate-Owned Work Profile, or Personally-Owned Work Profiles) with Always-on VPN enabled, VPN client Custom and the package ID, for example zscaler.com.zscaler.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector can restrict the traffic and secure the device before enrollment if Always ON VPN is enabled on your organization's MDM for Zscaler app.
After the app is enrolled, it intercepts the traffic and forwards it according to the policies in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Always-on VPN: Enable to allow Zscaler Client Connector to restrict the traffic and secure the device without enrollment.
Profile type: Select Device Restriction from either the Fully Managed, Dedicated, and Corporate-Owned Work Profile or the Personally-Owned Work Profiles sections.
VPN client: Select Custom.
Package ID: Enter your package ID (e.g., zscaler.com.zscaler).

variables-and-approval.statement: The Workspace ONE guide says Omnissa variables can be used for some Client Connector parameters, for example userName, and that selecting Keep approved when app requests new permissions automatically approves all future updates to the app. The MaaS360 guide says MaaS360 variables can populate the fields.

quotes: You can use Omnissa variables for some of the Zscaler parameters, for example, userName.
Select Keep approved when app requests new permissions to automatically approve all future updates to the app.
You can also use MaaS360 variables to automatically populate these fields.

mobileiron-enrollment.statement: In the MobileIron guide a device with a work profile or in Device Owner mode that is registered with the Android Enterprise configuration applied gets Client Connector installed and configured automatically, and users must open it once for the configuration to be applied the first time. The MaaS360 guide says users must launch the app and log in to enroll.

quotes: You can now register the device (that has a work profile or is in Device Owner mode) and apply the Android Enterprise configuration. Zscaler Client Connector is automatically installed and configured.
Users must open Zscaler Client Connector once for the configurations to be applied for the first time.
they must launch the app and log in to enroll in the Zscaler service

android-download-file.summary: The App Store downloads article calls the Android download on the Registered Devices tab an SDK file only, while the Workspace ONE guide downloads a Client Connector APK file from the Registered Devices > Android tab and says to contact Zscaler Support to enable the APK file link.

quotes: On the Registered Devices tab, you can view the released versions of Zscaler Client Connector versions for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android (SDK file only).

positions.says: The Registered Devices tab shows released versions for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android (SDK file only).

quotes: Download the Zscaler Client Connector APK file from the Registered Devices > Android tab.
Contact Zscaler Support to enable the APK file link.

positions.says: The APK file is downloaded from the Registered Devices > Android tab, and Zscaler Support is contacted to enable the APK file link.

android-download-file.impact: An admin who reads the downloads article may expect no APK on the Registered Devices tab, while the MDM guide downloads one there; the pages may describe different states, but neither says so.

always-on-restrict.title: What restricting the traffic before enrollment means under Always-on VPN
always-on-restrict.detail: The Intune guide says Client Connector can restrict the traffic and secure the device before enrollment under Always-on VPN. It does not say whether that blocks the traffic or only routes it through the app, and Android has no strictEnforcement install key (zcc.install.strict-enforcement:android-absent), so it is not strict enforcement.

sdk-file.title: What the Android SDK file on the Registered Devices tab is
sdk-file.detail: The downloads article says Android shows an SDK file only; no captured page explains what that file is or how it relates to the APK the MDM guides download.
